headline: Earnings surge on New Gold deal close; guidance reaffirmed
summary_short: Coeur Mining reported Q1 2026 revenue of $856.2M (+26.9% q/q) and net income of $246.8M ($0.35 diluted EPS), lifted by higher realized gold/silver prices and the March 20 close of the New Gold acquisition. Adjusted EBITDA reached a record $474.9M and cash grew to $843.2M.
summary_long: Revenue rose 26.9% q/q to $856.2M as 15%/53% q/q gains in realized gold/silver prices and new copper sales from the New Gold acquisition offset lower gold/silver ounces sold. Net income grew to $246.8M ($0.35 diluted EPS); adjusted EBITDA hit a record $474.9M. Free cash flow was $266.8M despite over $200M of deal-related outflows (performance-share settlements, tax withholding). Cash rose 52.3% q/q to $843.2M; total debt rose to $761.4M on assumed New Gold notes, and equity nearly tripled to $10.41B on acquisition stock issuance. Full-year 2026 production, cost, capex, and tax guidance was reaffirmed. Coeur also unveiled a $750M buyback (no shares repurchased yet) and an inaugural $0.02/share semiannual dividend starting Q2.

drivers.explanation: 15%/53% q/q gains in realized gold/silver prices and new copper sales from the New Gold acquisition, partly offset by lower gold/silver ounces sold at Wharf, Kensington, Palmarejo and Rochester.
Higher realized metal prices and post-acquisition sales drove the gain, partly offset by acquisition transaction costs, higher G&A/exploration expense, and higher income and mining taxes.
Fell q/q despite record EBITDA because of over $200M in one-time acquisition-related cash outflows, including performance-share cash settlements and stock-compensation tax withholding.
Equity nearly tripled q/q from common stock issued as consideration in the New Gold acquisition, which closed March 20, 2026.
Quarter dominated by the New Gold acquisition close (11 days of Rainy River/New Afton contribution), a new $750M buyback authorization, and an inaugural semiannual dividend.
